reading: The official tag string made no detectable difference - to similarity or to CER. Both intervals include zero and are wide (similarity -0.046 to +0.010, CER -3.4 to +7.2 points), so this does not show the tag has no effect, and it does not settle why v3 scored as it did. At the official recipe, on this development set and these metrics, MOSS v1.5 shows no detectable difference from the F5 baseline on speaker similarity (-0.013 [-0.053, +0.027], an interval that allows either direction); it is below OmniVoice by an interval that clears the 0.0205 reference line, and below MOSS v1.0; and its CER is clearly higher than the baseline scored in the same session - a recogniser measurement; nobody has listened, so how much of that is mispronunciation is not established. Its card says v1.5 with a language tag beats v1.0 on almost all supported languages; on this set's similarity measure that is not reproduced for Persian. Nine speakers, sampled renders, and metrics that are not the card's: a development-set finding, not a verdict on the model.
not_tested: the second official cloning mode - 'continuation' with the reference transcript, which the official app offers and the server docs say gives better speaker similarity; the transformers processor has no transcript field, so it needs the official app's own prompt construction

corrections.was: 'so v3's weak result was not the tag'; 'the render is unintelligible as the target sentence'; 'mispronounces clearly more than the baseline'; 'the recogniser behaved identically'
corrections.why: Independent review of 2026-09-19: an interval that includes zero shows no detectable effect, not the absence of one; CER and ASR transcripts are the recogniser's reading, not evidence of pronunciation or intelligibility without listening; identical baseline controls show the recogniser agreed on those 27 inputs only.
